en.name: Cashews, shelled
en.summary: Shelled cashews keep only 2–4 weeks from purchase in the cupboard, 6 months in the refrigerator, and 12 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). That very short cupboard figure is the point: cashews go rancid faster than almost any common nut.
en.pantry: 2–4 weeks from purchase in a sealed jar in a cool, dark cupboard — a fraction of what an almond gets, and worth taking seriously. Cashews are soft, high in oil and, because they are always sold shelled, their fat has been exposed from the moment of processing. Rancidity is the failure, not spoilage by bacteria: it shows as a bitter taste and a smell like old paint, and it happens quietly, without mould or any visual warning. Buy small quantities from a shop with fast turnover, and keep the jar away from the hob and the window.
en.fridge: 6 months from purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, in a genuinely airtight container. This is where cashews should live in most kitchens, given the cupboard figure. The fridge is humid and cashews are absorbent, so the seal matters: use a gasket jar, keep them away from anything strongly flavoured, and let the jar warm to room temperature before opening it so the condensation forms on the glass rather than on the nuts.
en.freezer: 12 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F), and for a big bag this is the obvious answer. Nuts freeze well because they contain very little water, so the texture is unaffected and they can be used straight from frozen. Bag them airtight with the air pressed out, and portion them, so you are not warming and re-freezing a large bag repeatedly. Roasting cashews from frozen works perfectly well.
en.thawing: No thawing is needed — use them straight from the freezer. For the crispest result, let the sealed bag come to room temperature before opening.
spoilage: A bitter, sharp, paint-like smell on opening the jar.
A soapy or bitter taste in nuts that look completely normal.
Soft, bendy or chewy kernels instead of a clean snap.
Mould or a musty smell in a pack that has taken up damp.
tips: Buy small and buy often; the cupboard window is only a few weeks.
Keep the working jar in the fridge and the bulk bag in the freezer.
Taste one before using a jar that has been open a while.
Let a chilled jar warm before opening to keep condensation off the nuts.

faq.a: 2–4 weeks from purchase in the cupboard, 6 months refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 12 months frozen at −18 °C.

faq.q: Why do cashews go off so much faster than almonds?
faq.a: They are softer, high in oil, and always sold shelled, so the fat has been exposed to air since processing. Rancidity is the failure.

faq.q: Should cashews be kept in the fridge?
faq.a: In most kitchens, yes. The cupboard gives only a few weeks, while the fridge gives 6 months and the freezer a year.

zh.name: 腰果
zh.summary: 去殼腰果自購買日起，放櫥櫃只有 2～4 週、冷藏 6 個月、−18 °C 冷凍 12 個月。櫥櫃那個很短的數字才是重點：腰果走油的速度，比幾乎所有常見堅果都快。
zh.pantry: 密封罐放陰涼避光的櫥櫃，自購買日起 2～4 週——只有杏仁的一小部分，這件事值得認真看待。腰果質地軟、含油量高，而且它永遠是去殼販售的，所以從加工那一刻起，油脂就一直暴露著。它的失敗是走油，不是細菌造成的腐敗：表現是入口發苦、聞起來像舊油漆，而且過程安靜，不長霉，也不會給你視覺上的警告。請少量、向周轉快的店家購買，罐子也要遠離爐台與窗邊。
zh.fridge: 真正氣密的容器放 4 °C 以下，自購買日起 6 個月。考量到櫥櫃那個數字，這才是多數家庭該放腰果的地方。冰箱潮濕、腰果又很會吸，所以密封很重要：用有膠條的密封罐、遠離味道強烈的東西，並且等罐子回到室溫再開，讓水氣凝在玻璃上而不是堅果上。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下，自購買日起 12 個月；買一大包的話，這顯然是最好的答案。堅果很耐冷凍，因為含水量極低，質地不受影響，也可以直接從冷凍使用。請密封裝袋、把空氣壓出，並且分成小份，這樣就不必反覆把一大袋回溫又冰回去。直接用冷凍的腰果去烘烤也完全沒問題。
zh.thawing: 不需要解凍，直接從冷凍取用即可。想要最脆，就讓密封袋先回到室溫再開。
spoilage: 打開罐子聞到發苦、尖銳、像油漆的氣味。
外觀完全正常，但吃起來帶肥皂味或苦味。
果仁變軟、可折彎或韌韌的，而不是清脆會斷。
受潮的包裝長霉或有霉味。
tips: 少量多次買，櫥櫃的期限只有幾週。
日常用的小罐放冷藏，大包放冷凍。
開很久的罐子，使用前先試吃一顆。
冷藏過的罐子先回溫再開，避免水氣凝在堅果上。

faq.a: 自購買日起，櫥櫃 2～4 週、冷藏 4 °C 以下 6 個月、−18 °C 冷凍 12 個月。

faq.q: 為什麼腰果比杏仁快壞？
faq.a: 它比較軟、含油高，而且永遠是去殼販售，油脂從加工起就一直暴露在空氣中。它的壞法是走油。
多數家庭應該放。櫥櫃只有幾週，冷藏有 6 個月，冷凍則有一年。
